claims.title: Legendary foundation of Rome
claims.summary: Roman tradition, fixed by the scholar Varro, dates the founding of the city to 753 BCE, with Romulus as first king. The date is legendary, but it long anchored Rome's sense of its own origins.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Italy: From the legend of Rome to a modern republic forged in the Risorgimento.", terralore.co/country/ITA/chronicle#ev-753bce-legendary-foundation-of-rome, claim TL:ITA:event:753bce:legendary-foundation-of-rome, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Greek colonies of Magna Graecia
claims.summary: From around the 8th century BCE Greek city-states founded colonies across southern Italy and Sicily, from Cumae to Tarentum, creating the prosperous Hellenic world of Magna Graecia.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Italy: From the legend of Rome to a modern republic forged in the Risorgimento.", terralore.co/country/ITA/chronicle#ev-740bce-greek-colonies-of-magna-graecia, claim TL:ITA:event:740bce:greek-colonies-of-magna-graecia, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Etruscan ascendancy in central Italy
claims.summary: The Etruscans developed a sophisticated urban civilization in central Italy and, by tradition, supplied Rome with several of its kings before being gradually absorbed by the Roman state.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Italy: From the legend of Rome to a modern republic forged in the Risorgimento.", terralore.co/country/ITA/chronicle#ev-600bce-etruscan-ascendancy-in-central-italy, claim TL:ITA:event:600bce:etruscan-ascendancy-in-central-italy, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Founding of the Roman Republic
claims.summary: Tradition holds that the Romans expelled their last king and established a republic governed by elected magistrates and the Senate, conventionally dated to 509 BCE.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Italy: From the legend of Rome to a modern republic forged in the Risorgimento.", terralore.co/country/ITA/chronicle#ev-509bce-founding-of-the-roman-republic, claim TL:ITA:event:509bce:founding-of-the-roman-republic, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: The Punic Wars and Mediterranean supremacy
claims.summary: In three wars against Carthage, Rome destroyed its great rival and became the dominant power of the western Mediterranean, beginning its rise to imperial dominion.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Italy: From the legend of Rome to a modern republic forged in the Risorgimento.", terralore.co/country/ITA/chronicle#ev-264bce-the-punic-wars-and-mediterranean-supremacy, claim TL:ITA:event:264bce:the-punic-wars-and-mediterranean-supremacy, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Augustus and the founding of the Principate
claims.summary: The Senate granted Octavian the title Augustus, marking the start of the Roman Empire. As first emperor he established the Principate and ushered in the Pax Romana.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Italy: From the legend of Rome to a modern republic forged in the Risorgimento.", terralore.co/country/ITA/chronicle#ev-27bce-augustus-and-the-founding-of-the-principate, claim TL:ITA:event:27bce:augustus-and-the-founding-of-the-principate, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Completion of the Colosseum
claims.summary: The Flavian Amphitheatre, the Colosseum, was inaugurated in Rome, a monument to the engineering and civic spectacle of the imperial city.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Italy: From the legend of Rome to a modern republic forged in the Risorgimento.", terralore.co/country/ITA/chronicle#ev-80-completion-of-the-colosseum, claim TL:ITA:event:80:completion-of-the-colosseum, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Edict of Milan and the rise of Christianity
claims.summary: Constantine and Licinius granted toleration to Christianity, beginning its transformation from a persecuted faith into the dominant religion of the Roman world.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Italy: From the legend of Rome to a modern republic forged in the Risorgimento.", terralore.co/country/ITA/chronicle#ev-313-edict-of-milan-and-the-rise-of-christianity, claim TL:ITA:event:313:edict-of-milan-and-the-rise-of-christianity, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Fall of the Western Roman Empire
claims.summary: The Germanic leader Odoacer deposed Romulus Augustulus, traditionally regarded as the last Western Roman emperor, ending Roman imperial rule in Italy.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Italy: From the legend of Rome to a modern republic forged in the Risorgimento.", terralore.co/country/ITA/chronicle#ev-476-fall-of-the-western-roman-empire, claim TL:ITA:event:476:fall-of-the-western-roman-empire, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Lombard invasion of Italy
claims.summary: The Lombards swept into Italy, fragmenting the peninsula into a patchwork of Lombard duchies and Byzantine territories and shaping its long political division.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Italy: From the legend of Rome to a modern republic forged in the Risorgimento.", terralore.co/country/ITA/chronicle#ev-568-lombard-invasion-of-italy, claim TL:ITA:event:568:lombard-invasion-of-italy, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Charlemagne crowned emperor in Rome
claims.summary: Pope Leo III crowned the Frankish king Charlemagne emperor in Rome, binding Italy to the Frankish and later Holy Roman imperial order and to the papacy.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Italy: From the legend of Rome to a modern republic forged in the Risorgimento.", terralore.co/country/ITA/chronicle#ev-800-charlemagne-crowned-emperor-in-rome, claim TL:ITA:event:800:charlemagne-crowned-emperor-in-rome, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Roger II crowned King of Sicily
claims.summary: Norman conquests in the south were united when Roger II was crowned King of Sicily, creating a wealthy multicultural kingdom of Latins, Greeks and Arabs.

claims.title: Lombard League defeats Frederick Barbarossa at Legnano
claims.summary: The allied northern communes defeated the Holy Roman Emperor Frederick Barbarossa at Legnano, securing recognition of communal liberties in northern Italy.

claims.title: Competition for the Florence Baptistery doors
claims.summary: The famous contest for the bronze doors of the Florence Baptistery, won by Lorenzo Ghiberti, is often taken as a symbolic opening of the artistic Renaissance.

sources.label: Florence and Central Italy, 1400–1600 A.D. (Heilbrunn Timeline of Art History)

claims.title: Medici ascendancy in Florence
claims.summary: Cosimo de' Medici returned to dominate Florentine politics, beginning the family's long patronage of art and learning that helped define the Renaissance.

sources.label: Italy from c. 1380 to c. 1500 (Renaissance, city-states, humanism)

claims.title: French invasion and the Italian Wars
claims.summary: The French invasion of 1494 opened decades of warfare in which France and Spain fought for control of Italy, exposing the weakness of its divided states.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Italy: From the legend of Rome to a modern republic forged in the Risorgimento.", terralore.co/country/ITA/chronicle#ev-1494-french-invasion-and-the-italian-wars, claim TL:ITA:event:1494:french-invasion-and-the-italian-wars, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Michelangelo paints the Sistine Chapel ceiling
claims.summary: Commissioned by the papacy in Rome, Michelangelo's Sistine Chapel ceiling became one of the supreme achievements of High Renaissance art.

sources.label: Florence and Central Italy, 1400–1600 A.D. (Heilbrunn Timeline of Art History)

claims.title: Napoleonic reorganization of Italy
claims.summary: Napoleon's campaigns swept aside the old states and spread revolutionary, legal and national ideas across Italy, before the powers restored the former rulers in 1815.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Italy: From the legend of Rome to a modern republic forged in the Risorgimento.", terralore.co/country/ITA/chronicle#ev-1796-napoleonic-reorganization-of-italy, claim TL:ITA:event:1796:napoleonic-reorganization-of-italy, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Garibaldi's Expedition of the Thousand
claims.summary: Giuseppe Garibaldi's volunteers conquered Sicily and southern Italy, bringing down the Kingdom of the Two Sicilies and clearing the way for unification.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Italy: From the legend of Rome to a modern republic forged in the Risorgimento.", terralore.co/country/ITA/chronicle#ev-1860-garibaldi-s-expedition-of-the-thousand, claim TL:ITA:event:1860:garibaldi-s-expedition-of-the-thousand, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Proclamation of the Kingdom of Italy
claims.summary: The first Italian parliament in Turin proclaimed Victor Emmanuel II King of Italy, the founding act of the unified Italian state and climax of the Risorgimento.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Italy: From the legend of Rome to a modern republic forged in the Risorgimento.", terralore.co/country/ITA/chronicle#ev-1861-proclamation-of-the-kingdom-of-italy, claim TL:ITA:event:1861:proclamation-of-the-kingdom-of-italy, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Capture of Rome
claims.summary: Italian troops breached the Aurelian Walls at Porta Pia and took Rome from the Papal States; after a plebiscite, Rome became Italy's capital, completing unification.

sources.label: Italy: The acquisition of Venetia and Rome

claims.title: March on Rome and Mussolini's rise to power
claims.summary: After the Fascist March on Rome, King Victor Emmanuel III appointed Mussolini prime minister, beginning the transition to a Fascist dictatorship.

claims.summary: Mussolini's government enacted antisemitic racial laws that stripped Italian Jews of rights and citizenship, foreshadowing later deportations under German occupation.

claims.title: Italy enters the Second World War
claims.summary: Italy declared war on Britain and France, entering the Second World War as Germany's Axis ally, a decision that brought defeat, occupation and devastation.

claims.title: Mussolini's fall and the armistice
claims.summary: Mussolini was ousted in July 1943 and Italy signed an armistice with the Allies on 8 September; Germany then occupied the north, and a violent civil war and Resistance followed.

claims.title: Birth of the Italian Republic
claims.summary: In a referendum, Italians voted to abolish the monarchy and establish a republic; the new democratic constitution took effect on 1 January 1948.

sources.label: Towards 2 June (1946 referendum and Republic Day)
